title_as_listed: CHEF iQ Sense | Smart Wireless Meat Thermometer | 3 Ultra-Thin Probes | WiFi Unlimited Range | 1000°F Heat Safe | 5 Sensors | BBQ, Grill, Oven, Smoker, Air Fryer | Gen3

editorial.dek: Three probes and a WiFi hub that reports the reading — the only product in the shop that keeps cooking while you walk away.
editorial.best_for: A whole bird plus sides, with the reading reported to your phone
editorial.catch: It is the only thing here that needs a hub, a network and a phone to tell you anything. Without those it is three expensive sticks.
check_before_buying: Confirm the probe count and the hub contents on the live listing — this model family is listed several ways (FLG-014).
Plan where the hub sits so the signal actually reaches it, and check the app works before the holiday.
Check how the probes are cleaned, and whether you would rather hand-wash three of them after every cook.

blocking_questions.question: Did the five people-supplied links mean these five products, or were they placeholders?
blocking_questions.answer: No — the supplied tokens do not identify products, and they were never meant to. Each token is 9 characters; an ASIN is a 10-character code, so a token cannot be one. The mapping in this register is what the links resolve to, recorded live on five separate occasions, four of which reproduced the mapping exactly (5/5 each time). The fifth, on 2026-11-20, saw one token land on the Amazon homepage instead of its recorded listing — logged as FLG-030, which neither confirms nor invalidates the mapping. Nothing public binds the short code to a product, so the intended fields stay blank and the observed target is kept in its own column. The intended fields are settled as “unknown”, which is a settled answer, not a gap in the record.

redirect_observation.note: Page title omits '[2025 Model]' and says 3 probes; products.json title includes '[2025 Model]'. Marketing-string drift only, no spec conflict.

faq: How many probes come with it?
The listing names 3 ultra-thin probes and a hub with 5 sensors, reporting over WiFi, with probes stated heat safe to 1000F. It also lists BBQ, grill, oven, smoker and air fryer among its uses.

The headline feature on the listing is WiFi reporting, so the reading arrives on a phone - which means the app, the hub and the router are part of the product. If you would rather not install an app, the instant-read in this shop is the other shape.

It is a marketing phrase on the listing. What it means is that the hub reports over your network rather than over a short radio link; how far the hub can sit from the cooker is a question about your router and your house, not a published number.
